session: consensus clock design v0.1 - open parameters

decisions_so_far.personhood: privacy-preserving proof of personhood, globally unique but unlinkable to civil identity (0.86)
decisions_so_far.clock_type: sustained supermajority: the clock measures readiness and shows only after a supermajority holds for a defined time (0.77)
decisions_so_far.custody: a publicly inspectable smart contract holds and pays the pool (0.64)
decisions_so_far.winner: a separate verified public vote after the clock ends entries (0.54)
decisions_so_far.direction: small pilot first (0.51), whose purpose is to test whether the legitimacy and representation problems can be fixed before scaling

design_principles: one person, one vote; all votes equal
a majority count must not erase visible opposition; the clock reports the opposition, it does not delete it
the mechanism measures consensus; it does not decide what is true
the pilot is a reality test: success criteria and metrics are fixed and published before it starts, and a mixed result is reported as mixed
pool_source: Candidate options are ours; choices, scores, and distributions are Jev's.

threshold_percent.instructions: What sustained supermajority threshold should the clock require before it shows that the competition ends?

criteria.60_percent: 60% sustained - the lowest supermajority; fastest to reach, thinnest claim of broad consensus
criteria.66_percent: two thirds (66.7%) sustained - the classic constitutional-amendment bar
criteria.75_percent: 75% sustained - three quarters; a strong claim of consensus, slower to reach
criteria.80_percent: 80% sustained - near consensus; powerful if reached, real risk of never firing
criteria.90_percent: 90% sustained - practical unanimity; the clock may never show

sustain_duration.instructions: How long must the supermajority hold continuously before the clock shows?

criteria.24_hours: 24 hours - one full rotation of all timezones
criteria.72_hours: 72 hours - survives a news cycle and a weekend
criteria.7_days: one week - survives weekly routines and one organized counter-mobilization wave
criteria.30_days: 30 days - survives a monthly cycle and sustained astroturf campaigns
criteria.90_days: 90 days - a full season; only truly settled consensus survives

pilot_measures.instructions: What exactly should the clock measure in the pilot?

criteria.support_for_a_future_picture: support for one concrete future-picture film, as in the real competition
criteria.trust_in_the_mechanism: participants' confidence in the clock mechanism itself
criteria.willingness_to_accept_outcome: participants' willingness to accept as legitimate an outcome they did not pick
criteria.all_three_as_separate_readings: measure support, mechanism trust, and acceptance as three separate published readings
criteria.readiness_to_end_a_shared_process: readiness to end a shared process, with no content at stake

pilot_electorate.instructions: Who should vote in the pilot?

criteria.open_web_proof_of_personhood: anyone on the open web holding a privacy-preserving proof-of-personhood credential
criteria.invited_diverse_small_group: 100-300 invited participants chosen for diversity of background and geography
criteria.existing_real_community: one existing real community that already has something at stake
criteria.two_ring_core_plus_open: a small invited core whose votes run the clock, plus an open outer ring whose readings are published but non-binding
criteria.representative_drawn_sample: a drawn, demographically representative sample of a defined population

sustain_break_rule.instructions: What should break the sustain - what happens when support dips below the threshold?

criteria.hard_reset_on_any_dip: any dip below the threshold resets the accumulated time to zero
criteria.hysteresis_exit_band: the clock keeps running while support stays above a lower exit band (for example entry at 67%, exit at 60%); a full reset happens only below the band
criteria.grace_window_for_short_dips: dips shorter than a fixed window (for example 6 hours) do not reset the clock
criteria.decay_instead_of_reset: accumulated time decays gradually while support is below threshold, instead of resetting
criteria.reset_only_on_sustained_opposition: a dip pauses the clock; it resets only if opposition itself sustains its own threshold

minimum_participation.instructions: What minimum participation (quorum) should make the clock's reading valid at all?

criteria.absolute_floor: a fixed minimum number of verified voters, smaller in the pilot and larger in production
criteria.share_of_registered: a minimum share of the registered electorate, for example 30%, must have voted
criteria.share_of_recently_active: a minimum share of participants active in the last 30 days
criteria.no_quorum_sustain_is_the_check: no quorum at all; the sustained duration itself is the only validity check
criteria.quorum_plus_spread: a participation floor plus a minimum spread across regions and groups, so a single bloc cannot carry the clock alone

pilot_success_criterion.instructions: What should the pilot's pre-registered success criterion be?

criteria.clock_completes_clean_cycle: the clock completes one full sustained-supermajority cycle without capture or manipulation
criteria.legitimacy_acceptance_rises: measured willingness to accept the outcome rises between entry and exit
criteria.survives_real_attack: the mechanism detects and survives at least one real sybil or capture attempt
criteria.honest_measurement_either_way: success is an honest published measurement of legitimacy and representation, whether the clock fires or not
criteria.participants_can_explain_it: a supermajority of participants can correctly explain what the clock measures

live_reading_public.instructions: Should the clock's live support reading be publicly visible while it runs, given that a visible countdown can create theater and feedback loops?
